metadata.title: Serial adaptive laboratory evolution enhances mixed carbon metabolic capacity of Escherichia coli

reference.title: Serial adaptive laboratory evolution enhances mixed carbon metabolic capacity of Escherichia coli

condition.medium: M9 minimal + 0.2% v/v single carbon per phase
condition.selection: fastest-growing progeny via mid-exponential serial transfer

trigger.observation: E. coli K-12 exhibits suboptimal fitness on glycerol and lactate, and prior single-carbon ALE studies showed such phenotypes can be reconfigured by evolution; whether sequential adaptation across two landscapes works was seldom explored.
trigger.reasoning: Evolve E. coli MG1655 sequentially on two alternative carbon sources to obtain generalist end-point strains and test serial-ALE as a strain-optimization scheme.
trigger.source_location: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (clonal ancestral population)

evidence.source_location: Wild-type MG1655 (fitness baseline); phase-1 ancestors LA/GL as comparators for end-point strains

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Outcome measured directly (growth rates, uptake rates, WGS of evolving populations).

alternatives.approach: Simultaneous mixed-carbon ALE (contrasted with Sandberg et al., 2017; avoided to evade trade-offs/bet-hedging)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Two-phase serial ALE: phase 1 ~800 generations on M9+lactate (LA) or M9+glycerol (GL); carbon switch at fitness plateau; phase 2 600-800 generations on the other carbon (LA-GL, GL-LA); 60 mL M9 in 300 mL flasks, 30 C, 200 rpm, transfer twice daily at OD600 0.4-0.6.

result.metric: Doubling time per passage vs cumulative generation; end-point SGR and CUR in each carbon source
result.after: End-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA acquired universal growth advantage on both single and mixed carbon sources without trade-off on the first carbon; GL showed trade-off in lactate (single-ALE specialist).

decision_chain.rule: When optimizing E. coli for utilization of multiple metabolically related alternative carbon sources (e.g., gluconeogenic glycerol and L-lactate), apply serial single-carbon ALE phases (~800 generations each to fitness plateau) instead of simultaneous mixed-carbon evolution, because sequential adaptation fixed carbon-specialist plus generalist mutations and avoided fitness trade-offs and specialist subpopulation splitting in the tested two-carbon system.

condition.sequencing: Illumina HiSeq 2500, 50-cycle SE, TruSeq DNA PCR-free library
condition.variant_calling: min coverage 10, min frequency 10%, CLC Genomics Workbench

trigger.observation: End-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA acquired universal growth advantage on both single and mixed carbon sources without trade-off on the first carbon; GL showed trade-off in lactate (single-ALE specialist).
trigger.reasoning: Identify causal adaptive mutations via whole-genome resequencing every 50 generations, using cross-study recurrence and ALEdb as causality priors.
trigger.source_location: Evolving populations of GL-LA and LA-GL lineages

trigger.observation: WGS revealed recurrent mutations whose individual and combined fitness effects were unknown.
trigger.reasoning: Quantify causal contribution of each adaptive mutation by reconstructing single and sequential (temporal-order) mutants in the wild-type background.

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Lambda-Red one-step inactivation (Datsenko-Wanner): overlap-extension PCR of mutant allele + pKD13 kanamycin cassette, electroporation into pKD46 cells, 50 ug/mL kanamycin selection, PCR verification, pCP20 marker excision at 42 C. 11 mutants (LA-GL set) and 7 mutants (GL-LA set); rpoC excluded (essential-gene engineering difficulty).

result.metric: SGR; percent fitness contribution = mutant SGR relative to end-point strain SGR
result.after: glpK variants = glycerol specialists (~40% of GL fitness on glycerol); rph-pyrE(del) = generalist (fittest on lactate, 2nd on glycerol); hfq generalist-like but antagonistic in combination; cyaA single mutant poor on lactate; ydcI variants negligible; glpK+ppsA synergy on glycerol (+15%); four-variant combination >80% of end-point fitness.

trigger.reasoning: Remove mutator phenotypes from LA and LA-GL before using them as bioproduction hosts.

result.metric: Genotype restoration (mutation-rate measurement not reported in main text)

decision_chain.rule: When deploying ALE-derived E. coli lineages as production hosts, check and restore DNA-repair defects (e.g., mutT/dam mutator alleles) before pathway introduction, because mutator backgrounds accumulated during evolution destabilize the production genotype - validated here only for lactate/glycerol-evolved MG1655 lineages used for acetoin production.

condition.media: M9 + carbon source + 0.2% Casamino Acids + 100 ug/mL ampicillin

trigger.observation: Plasmid-bearing strains showed delayed lag phase and low cell density (plasmid-encoded metabolic burden), and prior acetoin processes used LB or amino-acid-supplemented defined media.
trigger.reasoning: Enable acetoin production with glycerol or lactate as sole carbon substrate despite plasmid-encoded metabolic burden.

evidence.source_location: None reported for the supplementation choice itself

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Resulting growth and productivity measured directly.

alternatives.approach: defined media with exogenous amino acids (both cited from prior work)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Supplementation of production media with 0.2% Casamino Acids as exogenous nitrogen/amino-acid source.

result.after: Condition enabled growth and production on glycerol/lactate as sole carbons; plasmid burden (delayed lag, low density) noted.

decision_chain.rule: When producing acetoin in E. coli minimal medium with glycerol or L-lactate as the sole carbon source under plasmid-borne alsSD expression, supplement Casamino Acids (0.2%) as exogenous nitrogen/amino-acid source, because plasmid-encoded metabolic burden limits growth and prior acetoin fermentations relied on enriched or amino-acid-supplemented media.

engineering_logic_chain.initial_bottleneck: E. coli K-12 exhibits suboptimal fitness on glycerol and lactate, and prior single-carbon ALE studies showed such phenotypes can be reconfigured by evolution; whether sequential adaptation across two landscapes works was seldom explored.
engineering_logic_chain.hypothesis: Evolve E. coli MG1655 sequentially on two alternative carbon sources to obtain generalist end-point strains and test serial-ALE as a strain-optimization scheme.

rule_provenance.rule: When optimizing E. coli for utilization of multiple metabolically related alternative carbon sources (e.g., gluconeogenic glycerol and L-lactate), apply serial single-carbon ALE phases (~800 generations each to fitness plateau) instead of simultaneous mixed-carbon evolution, because sequential adaptation fixed carbon-specialist plus generalist mutations and avoided fitness trade-offs and specialist subpopulation splitting in the tested two-carbon system.

When deploying ALE-derived E. coli lineages as production hosts, check and restore DNA-repair defects (e.g., mutT/dam mutator alleles) before pathway introduction, because mutator backgrounds accumulated during evolution destabilize the production genotype - validated here only for lactate/glycerol-evolved MG1655 lineages used for acetoin production.

When producing acetoin in E. coli minimal medium with glycerol or L-lactate as the sole carbon source under plasmid-borne alsSD expression, supplement Casamino Acids (0.2%) as exogenous nitrogen/amino-acid source, because plasmid-encoded metabolic burden limits growth and prior acetoin fermentations relied on enriched or amino-acid-supplemented media.
